text:
anna: heads up — after flipping the INT8 KV compaction pass on the dedicated fleet we see memory growing with longctx workloads (seq 8k+) and a small but consistent accuracy delta on a few eval prompts. CPU/GPU profiles attached below.

mike: can you paste the perf numbers? is this only on one model+variant?

anna: repro on rwd-llama-70b-int8 and rwd-mistral-8x-int8, mostly on requests that have many distinct prefixes so KV reuse is low. quick numbers:
```
before: avg_rss=42GB, kv_pages=0.9k, avg_latency=112ms
after:  avg_rss=57GB, kv_pages=4.3k, avg_latency=125ms
eval-acc-drop ~0.6% absolute (some instruction-following prompts)
```

cheng: hmm, kv_pages jumped a lot — that suggests paging/eviction churn rather than a steady leak. do you have eviction counts and residency hist?

anna: eviction_count=23M over 6h, page_reuse_rate=0.12, compaction_cycles=3. I also saw an uptick in kernel selection fallback logs where we fall back from vectorized kernel to generic for seq>2048.

jess: low reuse + more pages sounds like fragmentation — compaction might be generating smaller free spans so allocator keeps creating new pages. Did the int8 compaction change page-size or slot packing?

anna: the compaction pass repacks slots to 8-bit contiguous blocks and attempts in-place freeing. It also sets a target_fill=0.75 which is different from prior 0.9. We thought lower fill would reduce eviction pressure but maybe increases fragmentation.

mike: does BF16 run show same pattern? maybe quantization interacts with kernel selection heuristics differently.

anna: ran BF16 variant last night: RSS went to ~46GB, kv_pages=1.1k, latency stable. No accuracy drop. So seems INT8 path triggers both memory churn and a subtle quality change.

cheng: can you share a stacktrace/profiler snippet for the compaction routine? also post the kernel selection logs (we log chosen kernel id per sequence length).

anna: pasted profiler bits:
```
# sample
compaction(ms): 14, 18, 260, 22, 310, 400
alloc_pages(ms): 5, 7, 9
kv_accesses_total: 12.4M
kv_eviction_total: 23.1M
```
kernel log excerpt: `kernel_select: seq=4096 -> kernel=vx_generic (fallback), seq=1024 -> kernel=vx_opt`

jess: those large compaction pauses (260-400ms) are suspicious. Could be lock contention during repack. If compaction runs inline with request path that could exacerbate latency. Do we run compaction in worker threads?

anna: compaction is currently triggered inline in the serving worker when its local fragmentation exceeds threshold. We have a flag to make it background but it was off for INT8 due to earlier correctness concerns.

mike: possible action plan: 1) enable background compaction for INT8 with a safe fence, 2) run an experiment raising target_fill back to 0.9, 3) instrument slot allocation size histogram and per-page free-span counts, 4) check if kernel fallback path causes extra allocations (maybe vector kernel reserves extra kv slots).

cheng: also probe batching heuristics — if the batcher groups many small prefixes into a single large sequence (via padding), we might be hitting fallback kernels that are less memory-efficient for INT8. Add trace to show batch composition per call.

anna: I'll run a canary with background compaction + target_fill=0.9 on a single shard and run seq sweep 512/2048/4096/8192. Will also log per-request batch composition.

jess: for the accuracy regression — check token-level logits diff (float vs int8 dequantized) and run the eval set with restored encoder state (force kv reuse) to separate caching effects vs quantization noise.

mike: if accuracy only manifests when pages churn (eviction), maybe the eviction/paging affects key ordering or numerical rounding due to page-aligned quantize boundaries. Not likely but worth checking.

anna: noted. initial quick diffs show larger KL divergence on prompts that reference long context. I'll attach full eval diffs once done.

sre-bot: deploy of rwd-llama-70b-int8 compaction-v2 -> canary shard 5 scheduled at 2026-03-18T03:40:00Z by anna.

anna: can we add a telemetry counter for `kv_compaction_blocking_ms` and `kv_page_reuse_rate`? we need to chart these over the canary window.

cheng: yep — I'll add the metrics and a visualization in console. Also add per-kernel memory-overhead metric so we can correlate kernel selection with RSS delta.

mike: last thought — consider switching INT8 path to prefer BF16 kernel when sequence length triggers fallback and we care more about stability than raw memory. Might be a temporary mitigation. BF16 cost is ~10% RAM vs FP16, but we saw it is much better than current int8 churn.

anna: agreed. I'll run the canary and post back perf traces + eval diffs in this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
